messages:
adele (Platform): FYI I hit a weird fallback regression this morning. Router sent traffic to model-variant A and then fell back to B, but the tokenizer mismatch caused tool-calls to fail mid-stream.

sam (Eng-Platform): Ugh. Any request id / repro?

adele (Platform): Put an excerpt below — request id r-17c9. Logs show token counts differing after reroute.
```
[router] INFO route_decision: chosen=gptx-16q-v2 fallback=gptx-8q-v1 reason=capacity; tokens_orig=842 tokens_fallback=895 tool_call_attempts=1 error=tool_schema_mismatch
[runtime] WARN kv_cache_miss: model=gptx-8q-v1 expected_kv_len=842 found_kv_len=895
```

sam (Eng-Platform): can you paste the router policy for that tenant? policy might allow cross-tokenizer fallback.

adele (Platform): policy snippet: `allow_fallback: true`, `fallback_tiers: [compatible, best_effort]`. This tenant is on tier=enterprise. I think we never validated tokenizer parity.

jonas (Eng-Runtime): tokenizer mismatch will reorder token boundaries -> kv cache indexing breaks. Runtime should detect tokenizer_hash change and either remap or reject fallback. Right now it just continues and that breaks tool-calls (function arg offsets).

maria (Eng-ML): tool-calling parity is another axis — even if tokenizers match, the function signature/serialization can differ between variants. We need a small compatibility matrix per variant: tokenizer_hash, max_context, tool_calling_schema_hash, kv_schema_version.

sam (Eng-Platform): agreed. Proposal: add a `compatibility` block on model-variant metadata and check at routing time. Example YAML for the matrix: 
```
compatibility:
  tokenizer_hash: "sha256:abcd..."
  max_context: 4096
  tool_calling: "stable-v1"
  kv_cache_version: "2"
  allow_fallback_if: ["tokenizer_match","kv_compatible"]
```

liz (Product): From a console UX POV we should surface the fallback reason (e.g., tokenizer mismatch) and recommended fix (pin to variant or accept best_effort). Customers should see cost/latency delta too. :eyes:

tian (Eng-SRE): Also need telemetry: increment metrics `fallback.attempts`, `fallback.rejected.incompatible` and tag with `tenant_tier` so billing attribution and SLA reporting remain accurate. If we silently swap models we should still bill against original routing decision for transparency.

jonas (Eng-Runtime): enforcement detail: runtime can expose an API `can_accept_fallback(compat_block)` that returns one of {accept, remap, reject}. `remap` would attempt on-the-fly tokenizer remapping + kv realignment but that's risky. Maybe only allow remap for minor tokenizer deltas (we can compute edit-distance on vocab indices).

maria (Eng-ML): For tool-calling mismatches, remap won't help. Need an exact `tool_schema_hash` match or fall back to not invoking tools and instead return an error/warning to the user. We should add a preflight check in the router.

sam (Eng-Platform): Thoughts on rollout? Start by blocking any fallback that doesn't have `tokenizer_hash` match and surface an override flag `--allow-incompatible-fallback` for emergency ops. Then collect metrics for 2 weeks.

adele (Platform): +1. I'll draft a compatibility gating RFC. Actionable items: 
- Add `compatibility` metadata to variant onboarding flow (eng-ml).
- Router: check tokenizer_hash and tool_schema_hash before rerouting (eng-platform).
- Runtime: return clear `fallback_reason` in response when mismatch detected (eng-runtime).
- Console: show fallback reasons and cost delta (product/console).
- Telemetry: emit `fallback.*` metrics with `tenant_tier` (sre/infra).

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by adele/rfc-214 on staging: deployment_id=deploy-7781 status=started :rocket:

sam (Eng-Platform): I'll add a small feature flag `router.fallback.strictTokenizers=true` behind an experiment. Start in staging and run traffic for the tenant sample.

maria (Eng-ML): I'll export tokenizer_hashes for current variants and compute collisions. Will upload CSV to the doc.

jonas (Eng-Runtime): If we need a fast mitigation, runtime can short-circuit and return `error: fallback_incompatible` to caller instead of silently continuing. That buys us time.

adele (Platform): Thanks all — I'll open the RFC and link it here: https://redwood.internal/docs/rfcs/compatibility-gating (WIP). Will also add the CSV and the YAML example.

liz (Product): Please include a simple copy for the UI explaining what 'incompatible fallback' means for non-engineers.

adele (Platform): ok adding that to the doc. Follow-ups: sam (implement router check), maria (metadata export), jonas (runtime short-circuit), tian (metrics), liz (UI copy).

sam (Eng-Platform): noted. I'll start the PR and ping for reviews. :thumbsup:

adele (Platform): end of thread for now — reopening if staging shows anything odd.
